content: A sleep log is a detailed record that documents an individual's sleep and wake times over a period of several weeks. It is primarily utilized to diagnose circadian rhythm sleep disorders and to assess the effectiveness of treatments for these disorders. A sleep log typically includes the following components: The time the individual attempted to fall asleep. The estimated time the individual believes they actually fell asleep. The number, timing, and duration of any awakenings that occurred during the night. The time the individual woke up in the morning. The time the individual got out of bed. The desired wake-up time the individual had in mind before attempting to fall asleep. Whether the individual woke up naturally, was awakened by an alarm clock, or was disturbed by external factors. Whether the individual got out of bed on their own, was prompted by an alarm clock, or was disturbed by external factors. A brief description of how the individual felt during the day, such as their level of alertness or fatigue. The start and end times of any naps taken during the day. A record of any medications the individual was using, if applicable. Sleep logs are often created manually, with entries hand-drawn on graph paper. However, specialized software designed for sleep log creation is readily available and can be used as an alternative. Spreadsheet or database software can also be employed for this purpose. Additionally, sleep logs are sometimes used in conjunction with actigraphy, a method that involves wearable devices to objectively measure sleep patterns.
